inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q3 2026 10-Q (460,423,326; basic shares on issue 459,272,300 at 30 Sep 2026, 459,275,445 at 22 Oct 2026). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. The 2027 exchangeable notes were irrevocably fixed to cash settlement in May 2026 and sit in debt. The 2030 exchangeable notes ($353.9M at ~$26.21 exchange price, $1,407.0M at ~$34.34) settle principal in cash (already in total_debt) and only the spread above the exchange price in cash or shares; both are out of the money at the current price and at the base value, so no shares are added. In the bull scenario the 0.875% notes would be modestly in the money (about $0.2-0.3/share of spread value), which is not modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026: cash-flow share-based compensation add-back $67.4M (9M 2026, Q3 2026 10-Q) + $23.8M (Q4 2025 = FY2025 $88.4M less 9M 2025 $64.6M) = $91.2M, plus 'Net share settlement of restricted share units' in financing $31.1M (9M 2026; Q4 2025 was nil). NCLH publishes no combined figure (its Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation carries only the non-cash expense), so the two lines are summed.
inputs.fcf_basis: last_fcf and reported_fcf are TTM actuals to 30 Sep 2026 (OCF $2,165.5M less additions to property and equipment $2,729.7M), not the FY2026 estimate. Reported FCF is structurally negative because newbuild deliveries are inside capex; it is not a distress signal by itself, but it is why net debt keeps rising.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), ERP 5.0%. Cost of equity ~13.5% at today's capital structure (levered beta ~1.8-1.9). Cost of debt ~5.5% pre-tax: blended book rate is ~4.5-5% (TTM net interest expense ~$680M plus ~$100M capitalised on ~$15.1B, pulled down by export-credit loans and sub-1% exchangeables) and marginal unsecured paper is 8.75% (Oct 2026 notes due 2031). No tax shield: the group pays almost no income tax. At market weights (equity ~$8.3B / net debt ~$14.8B = 36/64) WACC = 0.36 x 13.5% + 0.64 x 5.5% = 8.4%; at a de-levered 50/50 structure with beta ~1.4 it is also ~8.4%. Used 8.5% in every scenario - leverage and cyclicality risk are carried by the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not by a WACC premium or per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (liabilities $940.3M at 30 Sep 2026, mostly port facilities) are already expensed inside operating costs and therefore inside Adjusted EBITDA; they are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are inside total_debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered), routed as 'operating company, cyclical' via dcf-methods with the adaptations file read. A cruise operator is an operating company whose value is a cash-flow stream; it is not a bank/REIT/LIC, so debt is genuine net debt deducted in the bridge. FY0 = FY2026E: revenue $10,180M = 9M actual $7,918.5M + Q4 estimate ~$2,260M (Q4 2025 $2,244M, capacity up ~5%, net yield down ~4%); Adjusted EBITDA guidance ~$2.55B (25.0% margin) and Adjusted EPS ~$1.70. Year 1 = FY2027. STUB: the balance sheet is 30 Sep 2026 but the flows start 1 Jan 2027, and Q4 2026 is a heavy cash-outflow quarter (company-stated ~$1.1B ship-construction/growth capex + ~$0.1B non-newbuild for the remainder of 2026, against Q4 operating cash flow of roughly $0.3-0.45B on guided Q4 Adjusted EBITDA of ~$415M). That estimated -$850M is deducted in equity_bridge so the quarter is not skipped. CAPEX is the crux: revenue growth here is bought with non-cancelable newbuild contracts, so capex paths are the company's own dollar schedule (ship construction + growth $3.1B 2027, $1.8B 2028; contract payments $1.27B 2029, $3.27B 2030, $0.26B 2031, $9.8B 2032-2037) plus ~$0.5-0.6B/yr non-newbuild, converted to percent of each scenario's revenue - the same dollars in all three scenarios, because the ships get built whether or not yields hold. The terminal year uses a steady-state replacement rate (13-14.5% of revenue vs D&A ~11.5%) because ships are replaced at inflated cost. TAX: Section 883 and the Bermuda international-shipping exclusion keep cash tax near zero (FY2025 expense $5.5M); the path ramps 3% -> 5% of EBIT as a Pillar Two / Bermuda CIT allowance. WORKING CAPITAL: advance ticket sales ($3.14B) are a prepaid float, so capture is positive, but the balance has been flat for three years while revenue grew, so capture is set at 15% (base), not the ~30% the stock ratio implies. BUYBACKS: none since 2019; the flat share count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding. OCTOBER 2026 REFINANCING ($950M 8.75% notes due 2031 redeeming the 6.125% 2028 notes, repaying $380M of revolver and prepaying export-credit borrowings) is treated as debt-neutral; fees and any premium are not deducted (small). SBC is ~1.2% of revenue so the house/street band is narrow.

equity_bridge.item: Q4 2026 estimated free cash flow (stub between the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet and the FY2026 year-end the flows start from)
equity_bridge.note: Estimate, not a reported figure. Q3 2026 10-Q 'Future Capital Commitments': ~$1.1B ship construction and growth + ~$0.1B non-newbuild capex for the remainder of 2026 (of which ~$0.6B export-credit financed, i.e. it becomes debt). Q4 operating cash flow assumed ~$0.35B (Q4 2025 was $459M on Adjusted EBITDA of $564M; Q4 2026 guidance implies ~$415M). Replace with the actual 31 Dec 2026 net debt when the 10-K is filed and remove this line.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: capacity-plus-yield build (order book ~3.6%/yr net berth growth through 2037 plus ~1.4%/yr net yield), cross-checked against the FY2019-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 7.2%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Standard 3/5-year CAGRs are unusable: FY2020-FY2022 were the COVID shutdown (revenue $1.28B/$0.65B/$4.84B, equity fell from $6.5B to $0.07B). Revenue 3-year CAGR of 26.6% is a restart artefact; the 5-year starts from a near-zero base. EPS bases are negative. Equity 5-year CAGR is -12.7% (FY2020 $4,354M -> FY2025 $2,210M) and diverges from revenue by far more than 30%, so equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award taxes; no interest-income strip, the company is a large net debtor) has been negative in six of the last seven years: FY2019 +$69M, FY2020 -$3,629M, FY2021 -$3,362M, FY2022 -$1,708M, FY2023 -$890M, FY2024 +$722M, FY2025 -$1,282M, TTM Sep-2026 -$687M. No CAGR is meaningful on a sign-changing series. SBC plus equity-award taxes has been stable at ~$110-145M (1.2-1.6% of revenue since FY2023), so SBC is not the story here; newbuild capex is.

base.capex_note: Dollar plan converted to percent of base revenue: $3,600M 2027, $2,300M 2028, $1,950M 2029, $3,950M 2030, $1,000M 2031, ~$2,330-2,350M/yr 2032-2035, then 13.5% steady-state replacement in the terminal year.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% is 17.1x; the 15x cap binds. 15x unlevered owner FCF is ~7.5x EBITDA at a 30% margin, below the 8-11x cruise operators have historically traded at and below today's ~9x.

bull.capex_note: Same dollar plan as base over higher revenue; 13% steady-state in the terminal year.

bear.capex_note: Same dollar plan as base - the 13 effective ship contracts are non-cancelable - over lower revenue, so capex is a larger share of it; 14.5% steady-state in the terminal year.

scenario_narratives.base: The turnaround works partially. Capacity grows ~3.5-4%/yr as the Prima-class, Sonata-class, Prestige-class and the 5,000-berth Norwegian ships deliver against sales and charters of the oldest tonnage; net yield, which fell through 2026 (Q3 net yield $319.65 vs $341.89 a year earlier) with the booked position below the company's own optimal range, stabilises in 2027 and grows ~1.5%/yr once the base-loading pricing strategy and the new marketing platform reach 2027-2028 sailings. The ~$325M of identified cost savings and Great Stirrup Cay onboard spend take the Adjusted EBITDA margin from 25.0% (FY2026 guidance) back to the 30% the company earned in 2019, by 2032. Free cash flow stays lumpy and is negative in the heavy delivery years (2027, 2030); leverage comes down only slowly. The equity ends up worth roughly what the market pays today.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Elliott-backed board and new management close a meaningful part of the gap to Royal Caribbean. The booking curve is rebuilt by 2028, net yield grows 2.5-3%/yr on Regent/Oceania mix and private-destination spend, and unit costs fall as the cost programme lands in full, taking the margin to 33% (still below Royal Caribbean's high-30s). Cheaper refinancing as the credit improves is not in the unlevered flows but supports the multiple. Every dollar of extra EBITDA falls to an equity slice that is only about a third of enterprise value, so the per-share value roughly doubles.
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer downturn or continued share loss to larger, better-capitalised peers arrives while the order book is still being delivered. Revenue is flat in 2027 as yields fall to fill new berths, then grows only with capacity; the margin never recovers past 26% as fuel, EU ETS / FuelEU costs and discounting absorb the cost savings, and a Pillar Two-style change lifts cash tax. The ship contracts are non-cancelable, so capex does not flex and net debt keeps rising into 2030. On these flows the enterprise is worth less than the debt: the equity has no DCF value and what remains is option value on a recovery, with dilutive recapitalisation (as in 2020-2022, when the share count roughly doubled) the realistic path. This is a finding about leverage, not a forecast of insolvency - export-credit funding covers ~80% of each ship and the company says it has liquidity for the next 12 months.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: net debt is ~5.8x guided FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA, ratings are B1/B+, maintenance covenants apply, ~$19.4B of non-cancelable ship payments lie ahead, and the booked position is below the company's optimal range. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised at Q3 and the cost programme is concrete, so a return to the 2019 margin is the central case. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs yield recovery, full delivery of cost savings and no macro shock through two heavy delivery years, all under a management team less than a year old with a CFO transition under way.
probability_weighted.limited_liability_note: The engine does not floor a scenario at zero: the bear case is carried at its arithmetic value of about -$12.4/share, which makes weighted_iv ~ $14.4. Shareholders cannot lose more than their stake, so with the bear floored at zero the weighted value is ~ $17.5 (0.5 x 17.32 + 0.25 x 35.25). The canonical weighted_iv is left on the engine's unfloored basis as the conservative figure - the negative bear is a proxy for the dilutive recapitalisation that path would force on existing holders - and the floored figure is the upper reading. The same applies to the entry prices, which are negative in all three scenarios: no positive price earns a 15% unlevered return on these flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NCLH is an equity stub on top of a large debt stack: enterprise value of roughly $23B against ~$15-16B of net debt, so a 10% change in enterprise value moves the share value by about $5. The three scenarios differ mainly in whether net yield and margin recover to the 2019 level (base), beyond it (bull) or stall at the FY2026 level (bear); capex is the same contracted dollars in all three. The valuation is unlevered owner FCF at a single 8.5% WACC with the debt deducted at book. Because the equity is thin, the per-share spread between scenarios is very wide, and the probability-weighted value is a mean of a skewed distribution rather than a likely outcome. A 15% hurdle applied to unlevered flows is a demanding test for a business financed 64% with ~5.5% debt; expect the entry price to be far below the market price or not positive at all.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage amplifies every assumption: +/-1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $2-2.5 per share, and the terminal cap multiple (15x FCF, ~7.5x EBITDA) about $2.3 per share per turn.
Capex is contracted in euros (~EUR14.1B unhedged) and non-cancelable; a weaker dollar or delivery delays change both the capex dollars and the timing of capacity growth.

The terminal replacement-capex rate (13.5% of revenue vs 11.5% D&A) is a judgment about ship life and newbuild inflation; at D&A-level capex the base value would be several dollars higher, at 15% several lower.
The Q4 2026 stub (-$850M) is an estimate; the 31 Dec 2026 balance sheet will replace it.
Net yield is still falling year on year and the booked position is below the optimal range; FY2027 guidance (expected February 2027) is the first hard test of the base path.
Tax: the model assumes Section 883 and the Bermuda shipping exclusion persist. A loss of either is not in the base case.

Bear-case equity value is negative on a DCF basis (about -$12.4/share: enterprise value below net debt). It is included unfloored in weighted_iv (~$14.4); flooring it at zero for limited liability gives ~$17.5. See probability_weighted.limited_liability_note.
